target_customer: Analysts and business users without deep statistical training, such as survey and market research teams
problem: Excel was limiting for real analysis, while SPSS, SAS and R were daunting for non statisticians; the founder said there was a huge gap between Excel and the high end tools.

founders.name: Greg Laughlin
founders.background_notes: A startupbeat Q&A says he had used SPSS as a consultant doing basic survey analysis. YC page says he later started Campwing. Employer names and education not found.

founders.name: John Le
founders.background_notes: Education per the YC page. Prior employers not listed.

competitors.name: SPSS and SAS
competitors.what: High end statistical packages described as daunting for non statisticians
competitors.funding_then: Owned by IBM and SAS Institute

competitors.name: Microsoft Excel
competitors.what: Spreadsheet used for basic data exploration

competitors.name: R
competitors.what: Open source statistics language the cofounder found clunkier than Excel for basic exploration

technical_complexity.rationale: Choosing the right statistical test automatically and explaining results in plain English needed real statistics engineering, but within the reach of a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: The value was usability, which large vendors could copy; no data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: None copied it visibly; Qualtrics bought it in May 2016 as its first acquisition and merged it into the Insight Platform, with the Statwing service available until December 31 2016 per FinSMEs.

market_need_then: Founders cited their own pain with SPSS and R; Computerworld framed it as filling the gap between spreadsheets and high end tools. No usage figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used statwing.com, which now hosts an unrelated Thai language content site.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain English instead of stats jargon, per the YC description

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence found; a branding search returned nothing about Statwing.

brand_strength.rationale: A pleasant, memorable name and clear plain English positioning, but no sources show press on the brand, merch or community.

outcome_analysis: Statwing built a plain English statistics tool in YC S12 and stayed small, with a three person team at exit. Qualtrics bought it in May 2016 as its first acquisition, for an undisclosed sum, and folded it into its Insight Platform; the standalone service ran to December 2016. Funding was only YC and a few angels, so this reads as an early product acquisition rather than a venture scale outcome.
notes: Funding amounts undisclosed; aggregators show blank fields. Team size per TechCrunch is three at exit versus two on the YC page. The YC page names Greg Laughlin and John Le; Laughlin is the one quoted by Computerworld. Website statwing.com is now an unrelated Thai content site (dead for the original product). Computerworld article date not confirmed beyond 2012 launch period; as_of set to batch year.
